title: Not All Fallbacks Are Failures: Understanding and Recovering from Fallbacks in Mobile Voice Assistants
abstract: arXiv:2608.30738v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Robust understanding of user input is a core requirement for voice assistants deployed in real-world environments. In practice, these systems encounter heterogeneous fallback situations caused by noisy audio input, transcription errors, ambiguous requests, incomplete utterances, or unintended activations. Existing systems typically respond with generic fallback messages, which do not resolve the underlying interaction failure and can degrade user experience. We study fallback handling in a deployed smartwatch-based voice assistant for general health support in everyday environments. Our analysis is based on six months of real-world usage data from more than 500 users, yielding a dataset of 3,030 anonymized, naturally occurring fallback-triggering utterances. We contribute (1) an operational taxonomy and the annotated VoxFallbacks dataset of these interactions, (2) a comparative evaluation of different models within a classification pipel

translated_title: 并非所有回退都是失败：理解移动语音助手中的回退并从中恢复
translated_abstract: 对用户输入的鲁棒理解是部署在真实环境中的语音助手的核心需求。在实践中，这些系统会遇到由嘈杂音频输入、转录错误、模糊请求、不完整话语或意外激活等原因引起的多样化回退情况。现有系统通常以通用的回退消息进行响应，这不仅无法解决底层的交互失败，还可能降低用户体验。我们研究了一个部署在智能手表上、用于日常环境中一般健康支持的语音助手中的回退处理问题。我们的分析基于来自500多名用户六个月的真实使用数据，构建了一个包含3,030条匿名、自然发生的回退触发话语的数据集。我们的贡献包括：(1) 一个可操作的分类体系以及这些交互的标注数据集VoxFallbacks，(2) 在分类流水线中对不同模型的比较评估……
tldr: 该论文基于500多名用户六个月的真实使用数据，提出了语音助手回退交互的操作性分类体系并构建了标注数据集VoxFallbacks，以帮助理解移动语音助手中的回退情况并实现有效恢复。
en_tdlr: Based on six months of real-world usage data from over 500 users, this paper contributes an operational taxonomy and the annotated VoxFallbacks dataset to understand and recover from fallbacks in mobile voice assistants.
